summary: 1930 wooden CCC tower in the Ocala National Forest, replaced by a steel tower in the 1940s; fenced and deteriorating, with a roadside view on State Route 40.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-100 steel tower with R-6 cab (NHLR); flyer describes an eighty-foot steel structure

access.note: Surrounded by a perimeter security fence. Sources describe only a roadside view from a State Route 40 pull-off.

visit.trail_note: Small pull-off on State Route 40 along the Florida Black Bear Scenic Byway.

events.note: Original wooden tower built by the Civilian Conservation Corps, per the flyer. The Eastern lookouts page also says the CCC erected it in the 1930s.
Flyer says the wooden tower was replaced with a steel structure in 1946; the Eastern lookouts page gives 1949.
Flyer says the tower ceased operations in 1969.
Restaffed during heavy smoke that limited air detection, per the flyer.
Restaffed again during very bad fire seasons on the Ocala, per the flyer.
Registered July 24, 2016 as US 1136, FL 19; nominated by Robert Spear.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Flyer gives 1946 for the steel replacement; Eastern lookouts gives 1949 with no source. The story reports both dates. The record keeps only the replaced event, without a single year.

NHLR and the flyer both place the tower in the Ocala National Forest. The Eastern lookouts page names Apalachicola National Forest, a different forest in the Florida Panhandle, so that line is treated as an error in that source.
Flyer says the steel structure is eighty feet tall. The NHLR model name MC-100 does not state a height. The record uses the flyer's 80 ft (24.4 m) at medium confidence.
NHLR gives 150 ft (46 m), which matches the existing record. The flyer's 183 feet describes the vista the tower sits on, a different measure, so the record keeps the NHLR value.

notes_for_editor: The build and replacement history rests on one undated tourism flyer (about 2021, from the file name and its '91 years' phrase) plus a one-line Eastern lookouts entry. The NHLR page has no build date. Climbability is not stated by any source, so it is left out; the fence is the only evidence. Eastern lookouts names Apalachicola NF, which conflicts with NHLR and the flyer; treated as an error. Social-media photo posts were not used.
